Question ID: CW_U05_L05_GP_Q01

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

Publication context: A student finishes typing a rough draft and wants to place it in the class online publication space immediately. What should happen first?

answer.text: A. Post it immediately because typing means it is finished.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A typed draft still needs revision, format, and readiness checks.

answer.text: B. Delete the draft and start over.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The draft may be useful; it needs a publication workflow.

answer.text: C. Review purpose, feedback, format, audience appropriateness, and final conventions before publication.

feedback.text: Correct. Publication-ready work requires more than simply posting a draft.

answer.text: D. Change the title only and ignore the rest.

feedback.text: Incorrect. A title is important, but it is not the only publication check.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L05_GP_Q02

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

Collaborative publication context: Which role checks whether line breaks, paragraph breaks, title, and spacing fit the creative form?

answer.text: A. Weather reporter.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This is not a publication role. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Format checker.

feedback.text: Correct. The format checker reviews whether the piece's visual and structural choices support the form.

answer.text: C. Unrelated reader.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The role needs a specific publication responsibility.

answer.text: D. Person who changes the writer's purpose.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Collaboration should not erase the writer's purpose.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L05_GP_Q03

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

A peer suggests adding a loud dramatic ending to a poem meant to feel quiet and reflective. What should the writer do?

answer.text: A. Accept it automatically because all feedback must be used.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Feedback should be evaluated against the writer's purpose.

answer.text: B. Reject all feedback forever.

feedback.text: Incorrect. One mismatched suggestion does not make all feedback useless.

answer.text: C. Post the rough draft without revising.

feedback.text: Incorrect. The writer still needs a publication workflow.

answer.text: D. Consider the suggestion, then choose a revision that supports the quiet reflective purpose.

feedback.text: Correct. This uses collaboration while protecting the intended effect.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L05_GP_Q04

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

Which item best prepares an online reader before a creative piece?

answer.text: A. A clear title and a brief author note when context is helpful.

feedback.text: Correct. These elements can help the reader enter the piece.

answer.text: B. A random symbol instead of a title.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Random symbols usually do not prepare the reader clearly.

answer.text: C. A long explanation of every line.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Overexplaining can replace the creative work. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: D. No title, no formatting, and no final check.

feedback.text: Incorrect. That weakens publication readiness. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

questiontext.text:
Question ID: CW_U05_L05_GP_Q05

MLA Standard: MLA.CW.PUB.01

Which checklist best fits online collaborative publication?

answer.text: A. Type, post, ignore feedback, skip format.

feedback.text: Incorrect. This skips the publication process. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: B. Change everything peers suggest, even if purpose disappears.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Collaboration should support purpose. This choice is not supported by the provided context or lesson skill; choose the option grounded in the prompt.

answer.text: C. Check purpose, consider feedback, confirm format, prepare the reader, and complete a final readiness check.

feedback.text: Correct. This matches the publication workflow. This answer matches the lesson skill and is supported by the specific creative-writing evidence in the prompt.

answer.text: D. Only choose a font and ignore meaning.

feedback.text: Incorrect. Publication quality is not just visual decoration.
